researcher_notes: Could not pin a clean, citable year for when the IMPORT terminal unit was first publicly proposed. Eagle LNG's Jacksonville (St. Johns River) project is overwhelmingly documented as an EXPORT facility (DOE export docket filed Jan 2016; FERC EIS/authorization 2019). The only public import-infrastructure signal is President Sean Lalani's Nov 2019 statement that Eagle was prepared to spend up to $1B on LNG import infrastructure, while other commentary implies import plans dated to ~2018; sources conflict and none clearly frame a first-proposal year for an import terminal. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than fabricate; needs manual determination of which milestone GEM's 'Import Terminal' unit refers to.

Operating start = year the terminal began crude-oil export operations. Built and operated by Occidental as the Oxy Ingleside Energy Center, which commenced crude export operations in October 2016 (first VLCC May 2017); Moda Midstream acquired it 2018, Enbridge in 2021 (renamed EIEC). Single quasi-primary source (Port of Corpus Christi port-authority press release) verified for 2016; could not verify an independent second source (NS Energy 403), hence medium not high.

Operating start = year the Beaumont marine terminal was reactivated and loaded its first export cargo. Enterprise loaded the first refined-products export cargo from its reactivated Beaumont, TX marine terminal (Neches River) in May 2014. Two independent origins verified: Hart Energy (independent reporting) and the Enterprise press release (carried by digitalrefining; bulktransporter is the same release). Note: this is the export-reactivation milestone; the terminal complex itself is older.

terminal: Enterprise Houston Ship Channel Oil Terminal
researcher_notes: Operating start = year crude-oil export operations began at Enterprise's Houston Ship Channel oil terminal. It loaded one of the first post-export-ban US crude cargoes for Vitol (booked Dec 2015, loaded early Jan 2016) — among the first US crude export operations. Single source verified (gCaptain) tying Enterprise + Houston + 2016 to the first crude export; the terminal handled domestic crude before this, but 2016 is the crude-export-operations start. Original commissioning year of the underlying terminal is not documented independently. tier:low (single non-primary source).

EHT is a long-established Enterprise NGL/LPG (propane/butane/ethane plus petrochemical/refined/crude) marine terminal on the Houston Ship Channel with seven deepwater docks. Independent sources document only expansion years (e.g. LPG-export capacity expansions 2013 and 2015, refrigeration expansion announced 2024 for late-2026 service) — not the facility's original operating-start / first-export year. No verifiable single commissioning year found; leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guess. Needs manual/internal determination.

Operating start = year of first crude export cargo. EPIC Crude loaded its first crude-oil export shipment (Aframax tanker Eser K) from its Corpus Christi inner-harbor (IGC) dock on Dec 11, 2019. Two independent sources verified: Oil & Gas Journal and Port of Corpus Christi.

Operating start = year crude/condensate export operations commenced at the Seabrook marine terminal (Galveston Bay). An Aug 2018 announcement states export capabilities had 'recently commenced' (initial expansion was due online mid-2018) → 2018. Identity caveat: the terminal is operated by Seabrook Logistics LLC (Magellan Midstream / LBC JV); ExxonMobil is a connected crude shipper/owner, which is presumably why GEM names it 'ExxonMobil Seabrook.' Both verified URLs derive from the same Magellan/LBC press release (one underlying source), so tier:low / independent:false.

Flint Hills Resources' Ingleside crude-oil terminal at the mouth of Corpus Christi Bay. FHR is documented as having acquired the terminal in 2009 (acquisition, not commissioning) and the facility predates that; sources conflict on the relevant operating milestone (a ~2012 dock build-out vs. crude-export operations after the late-2015 export-ban repeal), and no independent source gives a clean first-operating / first-export year. Leaving UNRESOLVED rather than guess; needs manual determination of which milestone GEM intends.

substatus 'planned' = a PLANNED retirement, so the year is the planned retirement/decommissioning year. In April 2026 Freeport LNG filed with FERC to decommission/demolish its obsolete import-regasification facilities, requesting that the import authorization be terminated by no later than December 31, 2026 → planned retirement year 2026. (The import/regas terminal began operating June 2008 and effectively ceased after its last import cargo in Feb 2011, but the formal retirement is this 2026 decommissioning.) Two independent origins verified: LNG Prime (original trade reporting) and a Reuters-sourced report carried by energynow.com (also corroborated by Industrial Info).

Proposed year for Train 4 (T4). Freeport LNG filed its FERC application and commenced front-end engineering and design (FEED) for the proposed fourth liquefaction train on June 29, 2017 (FERC docket CP17-470; FERC authorization later granted May 2019) → first publicly proposed 2017. Single primary source (sponsor press release) verified, hence medium.
